sanskrit: vyāvartaye tatra rathaṃ nadīvegam ivārṇavāt avadhyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ manye yena te vikramo hataḥ
english: "I am turning the chariot back from there, as one draws it back from a river's torrent rushing toward the sea; for I deem that brāhmaṇa unslayable, by whom your valor has been undone."

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tato rājañ śanakair abravīd vacaḥ muhyate me manas tāta gātre svedaś ca jāyate
english: Then, O king, Dhṛṣṭadyumna slowly spoke these words: "My mind grows faint, dear charioteer, and sweat breaks out upon my limbs;

sanskrit: vepathuṃ ca śarīre me romaharṣaṃ ca paśya vai varjayan brāhmaṇaṃ yuddhe śanair yāhi yato 'cyutaḥ
english: behold too the trembling in my body and the bristling of my hair. Avoiding that brāhmaṇa in the fight, drive slowly to where the unfaltering one stands."

sanskrit: arjunaṃ bhīmasenaṃ vā samare prāpya sārathe kṣemam adya bhaved yantar iti me naiṣṭhikī matiḥ
english: "Reaching Arjuna or Bhīmasena in the battle, O charioteer, safety would be ours this day, driver—such is my settled conviction."

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyān mahārāja sārathis tvarayan hayān yato bhīmo maheṣvāso yuyudhe tava sainikaiḥ
english: Then, O great king, the charioteer set forth, urging on the horses toward where Bhīma, the mighty archer, was fighting with your soldiers.

sanskrit: pradrutaṃ tu rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya māriṣa kirañ śaraśatāny eva gautamo 'nuyayau tadā
english: But seeing Dhṛṣṭadyumna's chariot rushing away, O honored one, the descendant of Gautama then pursued him, scattering hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit: śaṅkhaṃ ca pūrayām āsa muhur muhur ariṃdamaḥ pārṣataṃ prādravad yantaṃ mahendra iva śambaram
english: And again and again the tamer of foes blew his conch, and gave chase to the fleeing son of Pṛṣata, as great Indra pursued Śambara.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ tu samare bhīṣmamṛtyuṃ durāsadam hārdikyo vārayām āsa smayann iva muhur muhuḥ
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, the unassailable death of Bhīṣma, the son of Hṛdika warded off in the battle, smiling as it were, again and again.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī ca samāsādya hṛdikānāṃ mahāratham pañcabhir niśitair bhallair jatrudeśe samārdayat
english: And Śikhaṇḍin, closing with that great warrior of the Hṛdikas, struck him in the region of the collarbone with five sharp broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu saṃkruddho bhittvā ṣaṣṭibhir āśugaiḥ dhanur ekena ciccheda hasan rājan mahārathaḥ
english: But Kṛtavarman, enraged, having pierced him with sixty swift arrows, with a single one cut through his bow, laughing, O king—that great car-warrior.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya drupadasyātmajo balī tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti saṃkruddho hārdikyaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Then the mighty son of Drupada, taking up another bow, enraged, cried out to the son of Hṛdika, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: tato 'sya navatiṃ bāṇān rukmapuṅkhān sutejanān preṣayām āsa rājendra te 'syābhraśyanta varmaṇaḥ
english: Then he sent forth at him ninety arrows, gold-feathered and keen-edged, O lord of kings; but they glanced off from his armor.

sanskrit: vitathāṃs tān samālakṣya patitāṃś ca mahītale kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena kārmukaṃ cicchide balī
english: Marking those arrows fallen short and dropped upon the ground, the mighty one cut through his bow with a sharp razor-headed shaft.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ bhagnaśṛṅgam ivarṣabham aśītyā mārgaṇaiḥ kruddho bāhvor urasi cārdayat
english: Then, his bow severed, like a bull with a broken horn, he afflicted him in the arms and chest with eighty shafts in his wrath.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu saṃkruddho mārgaṇaiḥ kṛtavikṣataḥ dhanur anyat samādāya samārgaṇagaṇaṃ prabho śikhaṇḍinaṃ bāṇavaraiḥ skandhadeśe 'bhyatāḍayat
english: But Kṛtavarman, enraged and wounded by those arrows, taking up another bow together with a store of shafts, O lord, struck Śikhaṇḍin upon the shoulder with choice arrows.

sanskrit: skandhadeśe sthitair bāṇaiḥ śikhaṇḍī ca rarāja ha śākhāpratānair vimalaiḥ sumahān sa yathā drumaḥ
english: And with the arrows lodged in his shoulder Śikhaṇḍin shone resplendent, like a great tree with its spreading, glistening branches.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ bhṛśaṃ viddhvā rudhireṇa samukṣitau anyonyaśṛṅgābhihatau rejatur vṛṣabhāv iva
english: Those two, having pierced each other sorely and drenched with blood, shone like two bulls that have gored one another with their horns.

sanskrit: anyonyasya vadhe yatnaṃ kurvāṇau tau mahārathau rathābhyāṃ ceratus tatra maṇḍalāni sahasraśaḥ
english: Striving each to slay the other, those two great car-warriors wheeled there in their chariots through circling courses by the thousand.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā mahārāja pārṣataṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ raṇe vivyādha saptatyā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Kṛtavarman, O great king, pierced the son of Pṛṣata in the battle with seventy keen, stone-whetted arrows feathered with gold.

sanskrit: tato 'sya samare bāṇaṃ bhojaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ jīvitāntakaraṃ ghoraṃ vyasṛjat tvarayānvitaḥ
english: Then in the fray the Bhoja, foremost of strikers, loosed at him in haste a dreadful arrow that brings life to its end.

sanskrit: sa tenābhihato rājan mūrchām āśu samāviśat dhvajayaṣṭiṃ ca sahasā śiśriye kaśmalāvṛtaḥ
english: Struck by it, O king, he swiftly swooned into a faint, and suddenly, overcome with stupor, leaned against his banner-staff.

sanskrit: apovāha raṇāt taṃ tu sārathī rathināṃ varam hārdikyaśarasaṃtaptaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: And his charioteer bore that best of car-warriors away from the fight, tormented by the son of Hṛdika's shaft and sighing again and again.

sanskrit: parājite tataḥ śūre drupadasya sute prabho prādravat pāṇḍavī senā vadhyamānā samantataḥ
english: When that hero, the son of Drupada, was thus overcome, O lord, the Pāṇḍava host, slaughtered on every side, broke into flight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śvetāśvo 'pi mahārāja vyadhamat tāvakaṃ balam yathā vāyuḥ samāsādya tūlarāśiṃ samantataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: He of the white horses too, O great king, scattered your force, as the wind, falling upon a heap of cotton, drives it on every side.

sanskrit: pratyudyayus trigartās taṃ śibayaḥ kauravaiḥ saha śālvāḥ saṃśaptakāś caiva nārāyaṇabalaṃ ca yat
english: Against him advanced the Trigartas, the Śibis together with the Kauravas, the Śālvas, and the Saṃśaptakas, and that host of the Nārāyaṇas.

sanskrit: satyasenaḥ satyakīrtir mitradevaḥ śrutaṃjayaḥ sauśrutiś citrasenaś ca mitravarmā ca bhārata
english: Satyasena, Satyakīrti, Mitradeva, Śrutaṃjaya, Sauśruti, Citrasena, and Mitravarman, O Bhārata—

sanskrit: trigartarājaḥ samare bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ putraiś caiva maheṣvāsair nānāśastradharair yudhi
english: the king of the Trigartas in the battle, encircled by his brothers and by his sons, mighty archers, bearers of manifold weapons in the fight,

sanskrit: te sṛjantaḥ śaravrātān kiranto 'rjunam āhave abhyadravanta samare vāryoghā iva sāgaram
english: they, loosing volleys of arrows and showering Arjuna in the encounter, rushed upon him in the fray like floods of water toward the sea.

sanskrit: te tv arjunaṃ samāsādya yodhāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ agacchan vilayaṃ sarve tārkṣyaṃ dṛṣṭveva pannagāḥ
english: But those warriors, by hundreds and by thousands, closing with Arjuna, all came to destruction, as serpents do at the sight of Tārkṣya.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare nājahuḥ pāṇḍavaṃ tadā dahyamānā yathā rājañ śalabhā iva pāvakam
english: Though slaughtered in the battle, they did not then forsake the Pāṇḍava, even as moths forsake not the fire that consumes them, O king.

sanskrit: satyasenas tribhir bāṇair vivyādha yudhi pāṇḍavam mitradevas triṣaṣṭyā ca candradevaś ca saptabhiḥ
english: Satyasena pierced the Pāṇḍava in the fight with three arrows, Mitradeva with sixty-three, and Candradeva with seven.

sanskrit: mitravarmā trisaptatyā sauśrutiś cāpi pañcabhiḥ śatruṃjayaś ca viṃśatyā suśarmā navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Mitravarman with seventy-three, and Sauśruti with five, Śatruṃjaya with twenty, and Suśarman with nine arrows.

sanskrit: śatruṃjayaṃ ca rājānaṃ hatvā tatra śilāśitaiḥ sauśruteḥ saśirastrāṇaṃ śiraḥ kāyād apāharat tvaritaś candradevaṃ ca śarair ninye yamakṣayam
english: And having slain there King Śatruṃjaya with stone-whetted shafts, he struck from Sauśruti's body his head together with its helmet, and swiftly with arrows sent Candradeva to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: athetarān mahārāja yatamānān mahārathān pañcabhiḥ pañcabhir bāṇair ekaikaṃ pratyavārayat
english: Then the others, O great king, those great car-warriors striving in the fight, he held off, each one of them, with five arrows apiece.

sanskrit: satyasenas tu saṃkruddhas tomaraṃ vyasṛjan mahat samuddiśya raṇe kṛṣṇaṃ siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca
english: But Satyasena, enraged, hurled a great iron lance, aiming it at Kṛṣṇa in the fray, and roared a lion's roar.

sanskrit: sa nirbhidya bhujaṃ savyaṃ mādhavasya mahātmanaḥ ayasmayo mahācaṇḍo jagāma dharaṇīṃ tadā
english: That fierce lance of iron, having pierced the left arm of the high-souled Mādhava, then fell to the earth.

sanskrit: mādhavasya tu viddhasya tomareṇa mahāraṇe pratodaḥ prāpatad dhastād raśmayaś ca viśāṃ pate
english: And as Mādhava was wounded by the lance in that great battle, the goad fell from his hand, and the reins as well, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: sa pratodaṃ punar gṛhya raśmīṃś caiva mahāyaśāḥ vāhayām āsa tān aśvān satyasenarathaṃ prati
english: That one of great renown, taking up again the goad and the reins, drove those horses on toward Satyasena's chariot.

sanskrit: viṣvaksenaṃ tu nirbhinnaṃ prekṣya pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ satyasenaṃ śarais tīkṣṇair dārayitvā mahābalaḥ
english: But seeing Viṣvaksena wounded, Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya, of mighty strength, having rent Satyasena with sharp arrows—

sanskrit: tataḥ suniśitair bāṇai rājñas tasya mahac chiraḥ kuṇḍalopacitaṃ kāyāc cakarta pṛtanāntare
english: then with well-sharpened shafts he severed from the body, in the midst of the host, that king's great head, adorned with earrings.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya śitair bāṇair mitravarmāṇam ākṣipat vatsadantena tīkṣṇena sārathiṃ cāsya māriṣa
english: Having slain him with whetted arrows, he assailed Mitravarman, and with a sharp calf-tooth shaft struck down his charioteer as well, O honored one.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatair bhūyaḥ saṃśaptakagaṇān vaśī pātayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then once more with hundreds of arrows the self-controlled one, enraged, brought down the bands of the Saṃśaptakas by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: tato rajatapuṅkhena rājñaḥ śīrṣaṃ mahātmanaḥ mitradevasya ciccheda kṣurapreṇa mahāyaśāḥ suśarmāṇaṃ ca saṃkruddho jatrudeśe samārdayat
english: Then with a silver-feathered razor-headed shaft that one of great renown severed the head of the high-souled King Mitradeva, and, enraged, struck Suśarman in the region of the collarbone.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃśaptakāḥ sarve parivārya dhanaṃjayam śastraughair mamṛduḥ kruddhā nādayanto diśo daśa
english: Then all the Saṃśaptakas, surrounding Dhanaṃjaya, crushed him with floods of weapons in their wrath, making the ten directions resound.

sanskrit: abhyarditas tu tair jiṣṇuḥ śakratulyaparākramaḥ aindram astram ameyātmā prāduścakre mahārathaḥ tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi prādurāsan viśāṃ pate
english: But Jiṣṇu, sorely pressed by them, equal to Śakra in prowess, the immeasurable-souled great car-warrior, brought forth the Aindra weapon; and then arrows by the thousand sprang into being, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: dhvajānāṃ chidyamānānāṃ kārmukāṇāṃ ca saṃyuge rathānāṃ sapatākānāṃ tūṇīrāṇāṃ śaraiḥ saha
english: Of banners being cut down, and of bows, in the encounter, of chariots with their pennons, of quivers along with their arrows,

sanskrit: akṣāṇām atha yoktrāṇāṃ cakrāṇāṃ raśmibhiḥ saha kūbarāṇāṃ varūthānāṃ pṛṣatkānāṃ ca saṃyuge
english: of axles and of harness-straps, of wheels together with their reins, of chariot-poles, of fenders, and of darts in the fray,

sanskrit: aśmanāṃ patatāṃ caiva prāsānām ṛṣṭibhiḥ saha gadānāṃ parighāṇāṃ ca śaktīnāṃ tomaraiḥ saha
english: of stones falling, of lances together with double-edged spears, of maces and of iron bludgeons, of pikes along with iron lances,

sanskrit: śataghnīnāṃ sacakrāṇāṃ bhujānām ūrubhiḥ saha kaṇṭhasūtrāṅgadānāṃ ca keyūrāṇāṃ ca māriṣa
english: of hundred-slayers with their wheels, of arms together with thighs, of neck-cords and armlets, and of bracelets, O honored one,

sanskrit: hārāṇām atha niṣkāṇāṃ tanutrāṇāṃ ca bhārata chatrāṇāṃ vyajanānāṃ ca śirasāṃ mukuṭaiḥ saha aśrūyata mahāñ śabdas tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: of necklaces and gold ornaments, and of corselets, O Bhārata, of parasols and fans, and of heads together with their diadems—a great din was heard here and there, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalāni svakṣīṇi pūrṇacandranibhāni ca śirāṃsy urvyām adṛśyanta tārāgaṇa ivāmbare
english: Heads with their earrings, fair-eyed, shining like the full moon, were seen upon the earth, like the host of stars in the sky.

sanskrit: susragvīṇi suvāsāṃsi candanenokṣitāni ca śarīrāṇi vyadṛśyanta hatānāṃ ca mahītale gandharvanagarākāraṃ ghoram āyodhanaṃ tadā
english: The bodies of the slain, well-garlanded, well-clad, and anointed with sandal-paste, were seen upon the ground; and that dreadful battlefield then took on the semblance of a city of the gandharvas.

sanskrit: nihatai rājaputraiś ca kṣatriyaiś ca mahābalaiḥ hastibhiḥ patitaiś caiva turagaiś cābhavan mahī agamyamārgā samare viśīrṇair iva parvataiḥ
english: With slain princes and mighty kṣatriyas, and with fallen elephants and horses, the earth in that battle became impassable, as though strewn with shattered mountains.

sanskrit: nāsīc cakrapathaś caiva pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ nighnataḥ śātravān bhallair hastyaśvaṃ cāmitaṃ mahat
english: There was no path for the wheels of the high-souled Pāṇḍava, as he slew his foes with broad-headed shafts and an immense host of elephants and horses.

sanskrit: ā tumbād avasīdanti rathacakrāṇi māriṣa raṇe vicaratas tasya tasmiṃl lohitakardame
english: The chariot-wheels sank down to the very nave, O honored one, as he ranged through the battle in that mire of blood.

sanskrit: sīdamānāni cakrāṇi samūhus turagā bhṛśam śrameṇa mahatā yuktā manomārutaraṃhasaḥ
english: The sinking wheels the horses dragged on with great effort, joined to mighty toil, though swift as the mind and the wind.

sanskrit: vadhyamānaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ pāṇḍuputreṇa dhanvinā prāyaśo vimukhaṃ sarvaṃ nāvatiṣṭhata saṃyuge
english: That army, slaughtered by the bow-bearing son of Pāṇḍu, turned its face away for the most part, and stood not its ground in the encounter.

sanskrit: tāñ jitvā samare jiṣṇuḥ saṃśaptakagaṇān bahūn rarāja sa mahārāja vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Having conquered in battle those many bands of Saṃśaptakas, Jiṣṇu shone forth, O great king, like a smokeless, blazing fire.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahārāja visṛjantaṃ śarān bahūn svayaṃ duryodhano rājā pratyagṛhṇād abhītavat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, O great king, loosing many arrows, King Duryodhana himself received fearlessly in combat.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā tava putraṃ mahābalam dharmarājo drutaṃ viddhvā tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: That mighty son of yours, as he rushed suddenly on, the King of Righteousness swiftly pierced, and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: sā ca taṃ prativivyādha navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena bhṛśaṃ kruddho 'bhyatāḍayat
english: And he in turn pierced him with nine sharp arrows, and, sorely enraged, struck his charioteer with a broad-headed shaft.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā hemapuṅkhāñ śilīmukhān duryodhanāya cikṣepa trayodaśa śilāśitān
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira hurled at Duryodhana thirteen gold-feathered, stone-whetted arrows.

sanskrit: caturbhiś caturo vāhāṃs tasya hatvā mahārathaḥ pañcamena śiraḥ kāyāt sārathes tu samākṣipat
english: With four he slew his four steeds, that great car-warrior, and with the fifth he struck the head of his charioteer from the body.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhena ca dhvajaṃ rājñaḥ saptamena ca kārmukam aṣṭamena tathā khaḍgaṃ pātayām āsa bhūtale pañcabhir nṛpatiṃ cāpi dharmarājo 'rdayad bhṛśam
english: With the sixth the king's banner, with the seventh his bow, and with the eighth his sword he cast down upon the ground; and with five more the King of Righteousness sorely afflicted the king himself.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tasmād avaplutya sutas tava uttamaṃ vyasanaṃ prāpto bhūmāv eva vyatiṣṭhata
english: Leaping down from that chariot whose horses were slain, your son, fallen into utmost distress, stood there upon the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ tu kṛcchragataṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇadrauṇikṛpādayaḥ abhyavartanta sahitāḥ parīpsanto narādhipam
english: But seeing him fallen into peril, Karṇa, the son of Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the rest advanced together, seeking to rescue the lord of men.

sanskrit: atha pāṇḍusutāḥ sarve parivārya yudhiṣṭhiram abhyayuḥ samare rājaṃs tato yuddham avartata
english: Then all the sons of Pāṇḍu, encircling Yudhiṣṭhira, advanced in the battle, O king; and thereupon the combat raged on.

sanskrit: atha tūryasahasrāṇi prāvādyanta mahāmṛdhe kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāśabdāḥ prādurāsan mahīpate yad abhyagacchan samare pāñcālāḥ kauravaiḥ saha
english: Then thousands of trumpets sounded in that great battle; war-cries and tumultuous shouts arose, O lord of the earth, as the Pāñcālas closed with the Kauravas in the fray.

sanskrit: narā naraiḥ samājagmur vāraṇā varavāraṇaiḥ rathāś ca rathibhiḥ sārdhaṃ hayāś ca hayasādibhiḥ
english: Men met with men, elephants with noble elephants, chariots together with car-warriors, and horses with horsemen.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvāny āsan mahārāja prekṣaṇīyāni saṃyuge vismāpanāny acintyāni śastravanty uttamāni ca
english: There were single combats, O great king, worth the beholding in that encounter, wondrous, beyond thought, full of weapons, and surpassing.

sanskrit: ayudhyanta mahāvegāḥ parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ anyonyaṃ samare jaghnur yodhavratam anuṣṭhitāḥ na hi te samaraṃ cakruḥ pṛṣṭhato vai kathaṃ cana
english: They fought with great impetuosity, each seeking the other's death; they slew one another in the battle, holding fast to the warrior's vow; for in no wise did they give battle from behind.

sanskrit: muhūrtam eva tad yuddham āsīn madhuradarśanam tata unmattavad rājan nirmaryādam avartata
english: For but a moment that battle was fair to look upon; then, O king, it raged on frenzied, as though deranged, and past all bounds.

sanskrit: rathī nāgaṃ samāsādya vicaran raṇamūrdhani preṣayām āsa kālāya śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: A car-warrior, closing with an elephant as he ranged at the head of the battle, sent it on to Death with smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: nāgā hayān samāsādya vikṣipanto bahūn atha drāvayām āsur atyugrās tatra tatra tadā tadā
english: And elephants, closing with horses, flinging many about, exceedingly fierce, drove them off here and there, time and again.

sanskrit: vidrāvya ca bahūn aśvān nāgā rājan balotkaṭāḥ viṣāṇaiś cāpare jaghnur mamṛduś cāpare bhṛśam
english: And having driven off many horses, the elephants, O king, swollen with might, struck some with their tusks and crushed others sorely.

sanskrit: sāśvārohāṃś ca turagān viṣāṇair bibhidū raṇe aparāṃś cikṣipur vegāt pragṛhyātibalās tathā
english: And in the battle they gored with their tusks the horses together with their riders, and others, seizing them with force, those exceedingly strong beasts hurled aside.

sanskrit: pādātair āhatā nāgā vivareṣu samantataḥ cakrur ārtasvaraṃ ghoraṃ vyadravanta diśo daśa
english: The elephants, struck by the foot-soldiers in their vulnerable parts on every side, gave forth a dreadful cry of anguish and fled in the ten directions.

sanskrit: padātīnāṃ tu sahasā pradrutānāṃ mahāmṛdhe utsṛjyābharaṇaṃ tūrṇam avaplutya raṇājire
english: And as the foot-soldiers fled suddenly in that great battle, casting off their ornaments and leaping swiftly down upon the field of combat—

sanskrit: nimittaṃ manyamānās tu pariṇamya mahāgajāḥ jagṛhur bibhiduś caiva citrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca
english: the great elephants, taking them for a mark, wheeled about and seized and rent the bright ornaments as well.

sanskrit: pratimāneṣu kumbheṣu dantaveṣṭeṣu cāpare nigṛhītā bhṛśaṃ nāgāḥ prāsatomaraśaktibhiḥ
english: And other elephants were sorely gripped upon their chest-plates, their temporal bosses, and their tusk-sockets by pikes, iron lances, and spears.
